bug_semantics: LiquidJS replace_first performs first-occurrence substitution by delegating to JavaScript String.prototype.replace (originally lodash _.replace, which is native String#replace). A string replacement is therefore a JS replacement pattern: $& expands to the entire matched substring, and $` / $' expand similarly. After memoryLimit landed, the filter charged only the input length (later input+args), never the expanded output. An attacker who can supply a Liquid template can chain assign plus replace_first with a replacement of many $& tokens, amplifying a 1-byte string through ~50x stages to hundreds of megabytes while the limiter records only the unamplified inputs, causing heap growth and event-loop DoS. Sibling replace uses split/join (literal $&) and replace_last uses substring, so only replace_first has this expansion path.
flaw_origin: The $& amplification primitive was first written on 2016-06-18 in 4595e2872e7800b93b0d6e487430431a0402f0b2 (filters: all), which registered replace_first as lodash _.replace at filters.js:30. Lodash 4.13.1 (package.json dependency at that commit) implements _.replace as nativeReplace.call(string, pattern, replacement), i.e. String.prototype.replace, so $& expansion existed from the first write. Immediate parent b478c798fdd5aba96b1fa279dd78410d4844584c has no replace_first implementation (only an unchecked README TODO). Later rewrites kept the same native-replace replacement-pattern semantics: 16a66f2b dropped lodash for (v||'').replace(arg1, arg2) while switching sibling replace to split/join; TypeScript moves and stringify wrappers did not change the call; e443068 (v10.15.0 DoS prevention) wrapped the existing str.replace(stringify(arg1), arg2) with memoryLimit.use(str.length) and thereby made the pre-existing expansion a limiter bypass. The 2026 fix 35d52302 changed the replacement to () => arg2 so $& is literal.

reasoning: CVE-2026-33287 is a published GitHub_M record (not withdrawn/rejected), so this is a real vulnerability, not FALSE_POSITIVE. The distinctive flawed mechanism is replace_first using JS replacement-pattern semantics (String.prototype.replace with a string replacement), which expands $& and therefore can amplify memory far beyond what memoryLimit charges. git log -L plus -S, excluding TypeScript/file moves, shows that mechanism was first written as liquid.registerFilter('replace_first', _.replace) in 4595e287; lodash 4.13.1 replace is native String#replace, and the parent tree has no implementation. 16a66f2b and later commits are rewrites/limiter wraps of that same call, not first-writes, so they are not the BIC. e443068 is when the incomplete limiter made the old expansion a documented bypass, but it did not introduce $& handling. The BIC is a 2016 human commit by harttle with no commit-object AI markers, hence NOT_AI. The direct fix is 35d52302, which lands in v10.25.1 as CVE.org states; GHSA's empty patched-versions field is not used as a withdrawal signal.
